query: Which white-box and black-box audio adversarial tests (e.g., PGD, bandlimiting, psychoacoustic attacks) are most informative for fusion systems?

response.query: Which white-box and black-box audio adversarial tests (e.g., PGD, bandlimiting, psychoacoustic attacks) are most informative for fusion systems?
response.answer: For fusion systems, black-box tests like bandlimiting and psychoacoustic attacks are most informative. White-box tests like PGD are also useful for evaluating robustness. These methods help identify vulnerabilities in audio systems.

results.title: Imperceptible black-box waveform-level adversarial attack towards automatic speaker recognition | Complex & Intelligent Systems | Springer Nature Link
results.content: # Imperceptible black-box waveform-level adversarial attack towards automatic speaker recognition. In this paper, we propose a new type of adversarial examples by generating *imperceptible* adversarial samples for *targeted* attacks on *black-box* systems of automatic speaker recognition. Inspired by *auditory masking*, a regularization term adapting to the energy of speech waveform is proposed for generating imperceptible adversarial perturbations. Experiments conducted on commonly used data sets, LibriSpeech and VoxCeleb, show that the proposed methods have successfully performed targeted attacks on state-of-the-art speaker recognition systems while being imperceptible to human listeners. Given the high SNR and PESQ scores of the yielded adversarial samples, the proposed methods deteriorate less on the quality of the original signals than several recently proposed methods, which justifies the imperceptibility of adversarial samples. On the contrary, audio files in adversarial attacks do not have to sound like the target victim but can also get access to the speaker recognition system, e.g., for white-box attacks in [8 Fooling end-to-end speaker verification with adversarial examples.
